leads.work: Each day an assistant forwards the vendor Energy Market Report (Economic Insight) by hand to a fixed list of traders
leads.why: Jill Chatterton sends 'FW: Energy Market Report' daily to the same ~12 traders. The list never changes, so the vendor could send to a distribution list or an automatic rule could do the forwarding.

leads.work: Every week Michelle Lokay writes the California Capacity Report by hand: TW and El Paso deliveries, % utilization and Gas Daily prices, all in a fixed template
leads.why: The same layout goes to the same recipients every Friday (02/08, 02/14, 02/22, 03/01, 03/08, 03/15, 03/22). The numbers come from systems and price feeds, so the report could be generated automatically.

leads.work: Reconciling pipeline imbalances and OBAs with El Paso (Mojave and CIG) by hand, month by month, with faxed daily volume statements and printed Location Quantity Summary lists
leads.why: Discrepancies going back to 1996 were worked month by month: faxes asked for and sent, reports printed by Richard Hanagriff, summaries re-sent, and the thread duplicated several times. Many differences were 1-2 units of rounding. An automated nomination/volume match between pipelines would avoid this.

leads.work: Time reports: an admin sends a reminder every pay period and each person replies by email with their absences
leads.why: Audrey Robertson sends 'Time Reports Due' over and over. Staff reply with vacation and sick days by email, and she corrects them by hand. Self-service timekeeping with automatic reminders would remove this.

leads.work: Weekly 'bullets' status collection from the marketers, including asking people with nothing to report to reply 'none'
leads.why: Kim Watson asks for bullets every Friday morning and requires a reply even when there is nothing. The answers are then forwarded on by hand. A shared template or tracker could replace this.

leads.work: Looking up monthly index prices (Mojave/Topock) by hand and emailing them on request, plus corrections when prices are revised
leads.why: Richard Hanagriff asks for monthly index prices. Michelle sends them in several pieces, and a revised February price had to be resent. A shared price feed would avoid this.

leads.work: Concur expense approvals sent to the manager by email notification, even for small amounts
leads.why: An approval notice for a $30 report that an assistant entered. This happens for every report, so routine approvals could be threshold-based or delegated.

leads.work: Moving staff to UBS: each person copies their own H/O/M drive data and exports their own email, signs a compliance certification on paper, and an admin collects the forms in a batch
leads.why: Many emails repeat or correct the instructions ('may not have been clear', attachments not saved on export). Each employee copies files by hand, and paper certifications go to Linda Guinn or are batched by Cara. This shows heavy manual effort and confusion.

leads.work: Account access set up by hand during the transition: production IDs and passwords emailed one by one (in plain text), EST account extensions requested by email with a business case, TDS access granted with a spreadsheet tool
leads.why: Separate access emails go to each user, EST account exceptions are argued out in long reply-all threads, and Russ sends an access application for staff to run themselves. There is room for automated provisioning, and passwords in email are a security risk.

leads.work: HR chases outstanding onboarding items (drug tests, benefits forms, orientation RSVPs) with individual emails
leads.why: Amy Fitzpatrick sends the same drug-test reminder to one person at a time and also sends orientation and form reminders. Onboarding tracking with automatic reminders would do this.

leads.work: Interview scheduling is collected by reply email (candidates email the times they are NOT available) and confirmed one by one
leads.why: Belden asks 16 applicants to email when they are unavailable, then confirmations go out one at a time.

leads.work: Meeting scheduling done through reply-all back-and-forth
leads.why: Several emails were needed to pick Monday or Tuesday for the Bakersfield meeting, plus similar exchanges for the Red Lake and CAS training sessions.

leads.work: Handing off risk and curve procedures between UBS and the Estate, with manual steps and workarounds in the curve manager
leads.why: Stephanie Hopkins asks for a list of procedures UBS people still run. The TDS curve manager has a button users must not press. Curve files are moved by hand. This suggests the process steps are not documented or automated.

leads.work: Checking test deals by hand in Tagg and Sitara for valuation booking
leads.why: Dawn Kenne asks people to review test deals by eye and reply by email. The check could be scripted.

leads.work: Daily real-time El Paso (EPE) model and schedule files saved to shared drives and sent by hand; CAPS settled daily (DA/HA finals)
leads.why: The EPE model is sent to Kathy by email each day and has file-path dependencies. The Estate settles CAPS every day. This looks like a recurring manual file workflow.

leads.work: Monthly meter volume recap prepared 'in the usual format' and tied by hand to scheduled quantities
leads.why: Clem Cernosek sends a meter recap in the usual format and works through exceptions with the operator. This recurring reconciliation is a candidate for automation.

leads.work: Capacity postings going up late, so shippers call before they are live
leads.why: Tammy says the posting went up late 'again', a repeated failure that costs time on phone calls. The TW Unsubscribed Capacity web page also needed several rounds of format and print fixes.

leads.work: Contract status tracking and amendments sent by email (CAF needed, tendered or executed status, name changes, MAXDTQ changes) through Contract Administration
leads.why: Craig Buehler sends a status list as of a set time. Customer requests are forwarded by hand to Dennis Lee, and contract admin needs a separate official email. Billing on expired contracts needs a CBS override. Lots of manual routing.

leads.work: Supporting applications that nobody uses (TW Deal Profitability and TW Deal Analysis)
leads.why: IT asked whether anyone still uses them. Marketing says no, so support can stop and save cost.

leads.work: Surveys of employees by email (club memberships) that require a reply from everyone, even those with none
leads.why: Jan Moore collects membership details one by one, with 'none' replies required. A form would be simpler.

leads.work: CAISO hour-ahead market notices and re-publications (GMM/TMM, TTC derates) that must be read and acted on
leads.why: There is a steady stream of automated CAISO notices. Schedulers have to watch them and resubmit schedules by hand, which might be automated.
